newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

If a proposed A$3.4 billion merger with the bottling arm of Philippines-based San Miguel Corp, Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc, proceeds, Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd will become the major bottling group in Asia. The move will allow Coca-Cola to start expanding into the lucrative Indian market as it takes over San Miguel interests. Page 23.

Industrial firm Wesfarmers Ltd is set to build a new A$150 million ammonia production plant at Kwinana in WA. The project will further the company's aims to build on its fertiliser and chemical base, and is expected to double its present production caacity. Page 24.

National Mutual Holdings group chief executive Geoff Tomlinson claims the insurance giant's end of year profits can be boosted by further cost cutting and the introduction of new product lines. To achieve this, subsidiary National Mutual Life is planning to launch a number of new insurance products aimed at overcoming a recent reduction in sales mainly due to increased competition within the life insurance industry. Page 25.

North Ltd has authorised a feasibility study, to be conducted through its Canadian subsidiary Iron Ore Co, into the possible re-opening of its abandoned iron pellet plant at Sept-Iles in Labrador, Canada. Interest in the project has been revived by a recent sharp increase in iron feedstock demand in North America. Page 27.

Emerging mining company Ross Mining has encountered local opposition to its controversial A$70 million Gold Ridge project in the Solomon Islands. Approximately 210 landowners from the Gaudalcanal region have expressed interest in joining a legal action opposing the project's establishment, saying they are concerned that compensation deals for local residents negotiated with Ross Mining will prove inadequate. Page 28.

Independent miner Trevor Kennedy has assumed the chair of Perth-based junior Kilkenny Gold NL. In opposition to current WA mining business practice, Kennedy has stated he will not direct the company to increase production to the maximum levels possible, instead he will seek profitable margins per ounce on lower levels of output. Page 31.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prominent businessman Simon Hannes was yesterday committed to stand trial on charges relating to alleged irregular financial dealings during last October's A$2 billion take-over of TNT by Royal PTT Nederland NV. Hannes will face further charges later thi month relating to his alleged use of confidential information to accumulate more than A$2 million during the TNT take-over. Page 21.

JB Were & Son managing director Terry Campbell last week finalised a A$1.5 billion placement by Were and ABN Amro Hoare Govett of a 31 per cent stake in Foster's Brewing Group. The sale of BHP's 617 million Foster's shares required a global offering, and the scale of JB Were & Son's role as broker effectively acting as principal has only been rivalled in business history by Goldman Sachs' A$2.5 billion dispersal earlier this year of a 3 per cent stake in British Petroleum. Page 21.

The Reserve Bank of Australia yesterday announced changes to the prime assets requirement, an important regulatory measure, that could see the release of over A$12 billion in funds for Australian banks. The RBA said it was reducing from 6 to 3 per cent the proportion of liabilities against which banks have to hold assets in the form of balances held at the Reserve Bank, Commonwealth bonds and notes and coins. Page 21.

The Federal Government will act to amend legislation eliminating the robotics and machine tools bounty. The decision has encouraged the computer industry to lobby the Government to pass similar measures protecting the computer manufacturing bounty, the only bounty of the four abolished in the 1996 Budget which has not subsequently been extended. Page 21.

Federal Transport Minister John Sharp confirmed yesterday that Australia will approach Singapore on opening bilateral talks on aviation issues, a move made a priority by Singapore Airlines' recent interest in acquiring an equity stake in Ansett. Other isues to be discussed include the further expansion of "beyond" rights for Australian airlines flying out of Singapore. Page 23.

Council of Textile, Clothing and Fashion Industries executive director Peter Kreitals said yesterday the Federal Government's decision to freeze car tariffs from 2000 to 2005 was the kind of decision the TCF industry had been lobbying for. Consequently, he industry is now calling for the Government to end the discrepancy in its treatment of the TCF and car industries. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

EnergyAustralia, the largest of NSW's six electricity distributors, could be broken up before the privatisation of the State's electricity industry later this year. Observers believe the move is aimed at making the giant organisation easier to sell, as its present valuation of between A$3 to A$6 billion may deter even large investors. Page 27.

ICI Australia has been thrown into disarray following the sudden death of managing director Warren Haynes, 58, who died yesterday after a "very short illness". Chairman Ben Lochtenberg will act as managing director until the ICI board meets to appoint a replacement. Page 27.

David Jones managing director Peter Wilkinson admitted yesterday the retailer is holding talks with its advertising agency Saatchi & Saatchi, amid speculation the latter is to be dropped from David Jones' A$15 million ad account. The Dalmatian dog campaign, promoted by Saatchi & Saatchi, which David Jones hoped would widen its consumer support has proved unsuccessful. Page 29.

Advance Bank plans to expand its Internet banking services using support from the Dutch designed Digi-Cash electronic cash system. Adoption of the new technology will enable the Advance Bank's 15,000 on-line clients to withdraw cash from accounts, convert it into electronic cash, store it in their PC and spend it on the Internet. Page 29.

Gold miner Plutonic Resources has announced a record monthly gold production for May of 52, 199 ounces. The publishing of monthly production figures is not common within the industry and results from Plutonics attendance at a gold mining conference held a Geneva, last night. Page 29.

Perth businessman Alf Binks, founder of Virtual Images Management and manager of the Large Format Film Trust, yesterday announced a bold A$61 million capital raising program aimed at producing large format films for giant cinema screens, used in Imax-style cinemas. The bid is being launched through a prospectus which offers 61 million shares at A$1 dollar each, and which fully informs potential investors of the risky nature of the venture. Page 29.
THE AGE

ANZ Bank chief executive Don Mercer and executive director Alister Maitland yesterday implemented a superannuation package that ensures they will retire with approximately A$2.7 million in benefits between them. The two exercised their share options on the stock market, taking advantage of a recent rise in ANZ share prices, to reap millions of dollars in profit. Page B1.

Financial markets have soared with stocks reaching a record high as a result of a strong night on Wall Street and the release of the ANZ job advertisement series which showed a rise of 8.6 per cent in job ads in the three months to May. Wall Street has rected strongly to last week's US employment data, which indicates future economic growth keeping profits robust without a rise in inflation. Page B1.

The Reserve Bank has been forced to cut the prime assets requirements for banks by half as a result of a shortage in Commonwealth Government securities. The PAR, which was introduced in 1985, includes assets such as notes and coins, loans to official shor term money market dealers, and Treasury notes and bonds, amongst others, will now be cut to three per cent. Page B1.

The management of chemical group ICI has been thrown into turmoil with the sudden death of chief executive Warren Haynes yesterday, with his death from "an extremely rare complication of a bacterial infection" leaving the leadership open. The natural choice for the top job is executive director Bob Hunt, but he will have to be convinced to stay in Australia as he is due to return to the UK next month. Page B1.

Macquarie Bank director Simon Gautier Hannes has been ordered to stand trial on two charges that he breached the Financial Transactions Reports Act by withdrawing and paying money in sums of less than A$10,000 in an effort to hide the purchase of TNT options last year. Hannes also faces another court appearance on June 30 on separate charges of insider trading in relation to TNT options. Page B3.

A survey into the upcoming telecommunications deregulation has revealed one quarter of companies believe deregulation will bring cheaper prices and boost competition, although they are not confident the change will bring improved services after July 1. It was also revealed businesses found it difficult to distinguish which phone companies were offering the cheapest prices, and they criticised the complexity of different phone deals on offer. Page B3.
